Musca: Petrus Plancius. Musca (Latin for 'the fly') is a small constellation in the deep southern sky.
Who is credited with discovering Testosterone?
Testosterone: János Freud. Testosterone is the primary male sex hormone and androgen in males.
Who is credited with discovering Cyanoacrylate?
Cyanoacrylate: Harry Coover. The cyanoacrylate group in the monomer rapidly polymerizes in the presence of water to form long, strong chains.
Who is credited with discovering Rubidium?
Rubidium: Robert Bunsen. Rubidium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rb and atomic number 37.

Belonging to the birch family and numbering about 35 species, these monoecious trees and shrubs are found across the north temperate zone, with a few extending into Central America and the Andes — name this genus of tree?
Alder are trees of the genus Alnus in the birch family Betulaceae.
This unit of length equals one ten-billionth of a meter, or 100 picometres, and is named after a 19th-century Swedish physicist — what is it?
Angstrom (ONG-) is a unit of length equal to 1010 m; that is, one ten-billionth of a metre, a hundred-millionth of a centimetre, 0.1 nanometre, or 100 picometres.
This American physicist won a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize for an effect, now bearing his name, that demonstrated light's particle nature — who was he?
Arthur Compton (September 10, 1892 - March 15, 1962) was an American physicist who shared the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics with C. T. R. Wilson.
The first production aircraft of its type, this American military transport combines vertical takeoff and landing with long-range cruise performance—what is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey is an American multi-use, tiltrotor military transport and cargo aircraft with both vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) and short takeoff and landing (STOL) capabilities.
This leafy vegetable forms no head, just green blades atop pale bulbous stalks, with a flavor often compared to a mix of spinach and water chestnut — what vegetable is it?

Bok choy (American English, Canadian English, and Australian English), pak choi (British English, South African English, and Caribbean English) or pok choi is a type of Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp.
This soft, silvery-white metal shares group 12 of the periodic table with zinc and mercury, resembling zinc in its chemistry and mercury in its low melting point — what element, symbol Cd, is it?
Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
Named for the whisker-like barbels many species sport, these scaleless ray-finned fish include some of the largest freshwater giants in Southeast Asia and Eurasia — name this diverse group of fish?
Catfish are a diverse group of ray-finned fish of the order Siluriformes (historically Nematognathi).
A notorious household nuisance pest that feeds on sleeping humans, this insect has never been shown to actually transmit disease to people — what is it?
Cimex lectularius is a species of Cimicidae.
Entering service with Strategic Air Command in 1960, this four-engine, delta-wing supersonic bomber was the first in the world capable of Mach 2 — name the aircraft?

Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight. To achieve the high speeds desired, Convair chose a delta wing design used by contemporary interceptors such as the Convair F-102.
A staunch defender of Georg Cantor's set theory, this mathematician co-founded proof theory and became one of the most influential figures in his field — who is he?
David Hilbert (23 January 1862 - 14 February 1943) was a German mathematician and philosopher of mathematics and one of the most influential mathematicians of all time.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.

It's the creation of economic value by spotting and commercializing opportunities — a venture that demands serious initiative and shoulders real risk. What is this process, named from a French word for the risk-taker who runs it?

Entrepreneurship is the creation or extraction of economic value by identifying and commercializing opportunities to deliver products or services, a process that typically requires considerable initiation and bears risk.
A legume plant from the family Fabaceae, its leaves and seeds have been common in dishes from the Indian subcontinent since ancient times — what is it?
Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is an annual plant in the family Fabaceae, with leaves consisting of three small obovate to oblong leaflets.
Son of a wealthy Greek architect, this 2nd-century physician and philosopher's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and neurology for centuries after his death — who is he?
This applied art and academic discipline uses text and images to craft visual communications aimed at specific audiences and objectives — what field is it?
Graphic design is a profession, academic discipline and applied art that involves creating visual communications intended to transmit specific messages to social groups, with specific objectives.
Credited with putting middle-class Americans behind the wheel, this industrialist lent his surname to the very philosophy of assembly-line manufacturing. Who is he?
Henry Ford (July 30, 1863 - April 7, 1947) was an American industrialist and business magnate.
This endocrine condition floods the body with thyroid hormone, causing a racing heart, heat intolerance, tremor, and weight loss — and a rare 'storm' can be deadly; what is it?
Hyperthyroidism is a endocrine disease in which the thyroid gland produces excessive amounts of thyroid hormones.

A colorless, flammable organic compound with a pungent odor, this liquid is miscible in water, ethanol, and chloroform, and is widely used as a solvent and disinfectant. It's commonly abbreviated as IPA—what is it?
Isopropyl alcohol (IUPAC name propan-2-ol and also called isopropanol or 2-propanol, commonly abbreviated as IPA) is a colorless, flammable, organic compound with a pungent odor.

An Alberta-raised classical liberal who earned his PhD in clinical psychology at McGill and taught at Harvard before the University of Toronto, this commentator drew huge attention in the late 2010s — who is he?
Jordan Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.
This American economist served as U.S. Treasury Secretary, later led the National Economic Council, and was the 27th president of Harvard before resigning a professorship there in 2026 — who is he?
Larry Summers (born November 30, 1954) is an American economist.
Known mainly from fossils in Peru's Pisco Formation, this Miocene-era macroraptorial sperm whale takes its name from a biblical sea monster — what is it called?
Livyatan is an extinct genus of highly predatory macroraptorial sperm whale, containing one known species: L. melvillei.
Its Spanish name translates to 'little apple of death' — this tropical tree's apple-like fruit and toxic milky sap make it one of the most poisonous trees on Earth — which tree?
Manchineel (Hippomane mancinella), also known as the tree of death, is a species of flowering plant in the spurge family (Euphorbiaceae).

Patented in 1922 and used to relieve pain, fever, and spasms, this drug's sale is restricted in some countries due to a rare but serious blood-cell side effect discovered in the 1970s — what drug is it?
Metamizole is a painkiller, spasm reliever, and fever reliever drug.
First synthesized in 2003 by Russian and American scientists at Dubna, this synthetic element — atomic number 115 — was named in 2016 for the oblast around its birthplace — what is it?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Found in tiny native amounts in Earth's crust but riding inside iron meteorites that never met oxygen, this hard, ductile metal shares its name with a small coin — which element is it?
Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
These red-haired great apes once roamed all of Southeast Asia but now cling to just Borneo and Sumatra — and in 2017 scientists confirmed a brand-new third species among them. Which animal is it?
Orangutan are great apes native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia.
Which American biologist became famous for the controversial 1968 book 'The Population Bomb' and its dire warnings about population growth, famine, and resource depletion?

Paul R. Ehrlich (May 29, 1932 - March 13, 2026) was an American biologist, author, and environmentalist known for his predictions and warnings about the consequences of population growth, including famine and resource depletion.

This class of lipid molecules has a water-loving 'head' built around a phosphate group and two water-fearing fatty-acid 'tails' — and forms an essential building block of neuronal membranes in the brain. Name the class of molecule?

Phospholipid are a class of lipids whose molecule has a hydrophilic "head" containing a phosphate group and two hydrophobic "tails" derived from fatty acids, joined by an alcohol residue (usually a glycerol molecule).
Known as little hogweed or pursley, every part of this succulent plant can be eaten raw or cooked — what plant is it?
Portulaca oleracea (common purslane, also known as little hogweed, or pursley) is a succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae.
This set of three positive whole numbers, like (3, 4, 5), satisfies a squared plus b squared equals c squared and forms the side lengths of a right triangle — what is it called?
Pythagorean triple consists of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a2 + b2 = c2.
As chairman of the now-defunct Purdue Pharma, he oversaw the launch of OxyContin — a tenure dramatized in Hulu's Dopesick and Netflix's Painkiller; who is he?
Richard Sackler (born March 10, 1945) is an American businessman, pharmaceutical entrepreneur and physician who was the chairman and president of Purdue Pharma, a now-defunct pharmaceutical company.

Often striking suddenly after heavy lifting and described as a shooting pain down one leg, about 90% of cases trace to a spinal disc herniation pressing on a nerve root — what's this condition called?
Sciatica is pain going down the leg from the lower back.
This Irish mathematician and physicist held Cambridge's Lucasian chair for a record 54 years and lent his name to a theorem in vector calculus and to equations of fluid motion — who was he?
Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet (stohks; 13 August 1819 - 1 February 1903), was an Irish mathematician and physicist.
This round, gram-positive germ lives harmlessly on most people's skin and noses, but turn opportunistic and it triggers abscesses, sinus infections, and food poisoning. What is it?

Staphylococcus aureus is a gram-positive spherically shaped bacterium, a member of the Bacillota, and is a usual member of the microbiota of the body, frequently found in the upper respiratory tract and on the skin.
These large, often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae number over a thousand species, and New World pet varieties can flick irritating 'urticating hairs' at threats. What creatures are they?
Tarantula are a group of large and often hairy spiders of the family Theraphosidae.

Affecting roughly 10 to 15 percent of people, this condition causes a person to hear ringing or other sounds with no external source, and its name comes from the Latin word for 'to ring' — what is it?
Tinnitus is a condition when a person hears a ringing sound or a different variety of sounds when no corresponding external sound is present and that other people cannot hear.
This medical specialty, whose name derives from the Greek word for urine, covers surgical and medical treatment of the urinary tract and the male reproductive organs — name this field?

Urology (from Greek ouron "urine" and - -logia "study of"), also known as genitourinary surgery, is the branch of medicine that focuses on surgical and medical diseases of the urinary system and the male reproductive organs.
The first-ever recipient of the Nobel Prize in Physics, this German scientist discovered a form of electromagnetic radiation named after him in some languages — who was he?

Wilhelm Röntgen (27 March 1845 - 10 February 1923) was a German experimental physicist who produced and detected electromagnetic radiation in a wavelength range known as X-rays (known as Rntgen rays in many languages).

Best known for the Cities of Salt quintet chronicling how oil discovery upended traditional Bedouin life, this novelist's criticism of Middle Eastern elites led Saudi Arabia to revoke his citizenship — who is he?

Originally launched in 2008 as Bombardier's CSeries, this five-abreast narrow-body airliner family was rebranded in 2018 after a European aerospace giant acquired a majority stake. What's it called today?
Airbus A220: Canadian narrow-body airliner family. The Airbus A220 is a family of five-abreast narrow-body airliners by Airbus Canada Limited Partnership (ACLP).
This three-star system includes Proxima, the closest star to the Sun, and shines as the third-brightest point in the night sky after Sirius and Canopus — which system?
Alpha Centauri: Star system in the Centaurus constellation.
Likened to a bubble or balloon, this outward bulge forms at a weak spot in a blood-vessel wall and grows ever more dangerous as it risks rupture — what is it?
Aneurysm: Bulge in the wall of a blood vessel. An aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
Sold under the brand name Strattera, this selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats ADHD and is only recommended for patients age six and up — what is this medication?
Atomoxetine: Medication used to treat ADHD.
A blood-feeding parasite of the genus Cimex that usually bites at night, this insect leaves itchy welts but, reassuringly, isn't known to spread any infectious disease — what is it?
Bed bug: Type of insect that feeds on human blood.

Also nicknamed 'buffalo gnats' or 'turkey gnats,' these small biting insects in the family Simuliidae feed mainly on nectar, though females also drink blood from birds and mammals — what are they called?
Black fly: Family of insects. Black flies or blackflies (sometimes called buffalo gnats, turkey gnats, or white socks) are flies in the family Simuliidae of the Culicomorpha infraorder.

This rare and potentially fatal illness comes from a toxin better known by its cosmetic nickname; it starts with blurry vision and slurred speech but usually spares both fever and consciousness — what is it?
First proposed after the 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese, this psychological theory says people are less likely to help a victim when others are present — what's it called?
Bystander effect: Social psychological theory. Recent research has focused on "real world" events captured on security cameras, and the coherency and robustness of the effect has come under question.

This polyatomic ion, CO3 with a 2- charge, is dissolved into water under pressure to make it fizzy, and also makes up much of the sedimentary rock in the Earth's crust — what's the ion (and salt) called?
Carbonate: Salt or ester of carbonic acid.
Discovered in 1945 and first sold in 1964, this class of beta-lactam antibiotics was originally pulled from a fungus once known as Cephalosporium — what's the family called?
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
The smallest member of the cockatoo family and native to Australia, this crested pet bird is kept in an estimated 4.8 million US households — what bird is it?
Cockatiel: Species of bird. It is, therefore, now classified as the smallest subfamily of the Cacatuidae (cockatoo family).
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
Caused by about 40 types of fungus and often picked up in public showers or contact sports like wrestling, this infection produces a red, itchy, scaly circular rash — what is it?
Dermatophytosis: Fungus infection of the skin. Dermatophytosis, also known as tinea and ringworm, is a fungal infection of the skin (a dermatomycosis), that may affect skin, hair, and nails.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, this ground-dwelling insect hears through an organ on its abdomen and leaps away from danger using powerful hind legs — what is it?
Grasshopper: Common name for a group of insects.

This Austrian physician who coined "autistic psychopathy" lent his name to a syndrome, but later faced allegations he referred disabled children to a Vienna clinic that killed hundreds during the Nazi era — who was he?
This seasonal state of drastically reduced metabolism, breathing, and heart rate lets animals conserve energy through winter months, with 'aestivation' as its summer counterpart — what is it called?
Hibernation: Physiological state of dormant inactivity in order to pass the winter season.
This poisonous gas or liquid with the formula HF dissolves in water to form a corrosive acid and serves as the chief industrial source of fluorine — what is it?

Named for the indigo-blue line seen in its spectrum when discovered in 1863, this soft, silvery-white metal with atomic number 49 is used to make the transparent conductive coating on flat-panel displays — what is it?
Indium: Chemical element with atomic number 49 (In)

His 1962 book The Calculus of Consent launched a theory of how politicians' and bureaucrats' self-interest shapes their decisions, earning him the 1986 Nobel in economics — which founder of public choice theory is this?
James M. Buchanan: American economist and Nobel Laureate (1919–2013)
Dubbed the 'Angel of Death,' this German physician held doctorates in both anthropology and medicine before joining the SS and selecting Auschwitz prisoners for the gas chambers — who was he?
Josef Mengele: Nazi SS doctor at Auschwitz (1911–1979)
Bred for their dazzling colors since the early 19th century in Niigata, Japan, these ornamental carp come in patterns like Kōhaku and Shōwa Sanshoku — what are they?
Koi: Colored varieties of Amur carp.
Distinguished by coloured scales, large triangular wings, and a nectar-sipping proboscis, which insect order encompasses both butterflies and moths?
Lepidoptera: Order of insects including moths and butterflies.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
This German physicist won the 1914 Nobel for discovering how crystals diffract X-rays, then — a fierce opponent of Nazism — helped rebuild German science after the war. Who is he?
This colorless gas, made by swapping one hydrogen atom in ammonia for a methyl group, has a strong rotten-fish smell and serves as a building block for many compounds — what is it?

An Egyptian-born civil engineer and architect who studied in Cairo and Germany, at 33 he was the oldest of the 19 hijackers and the ringleader who piloted American Airlines Flight 11 into the North Tower — who was he?
Mohamed Atta: Egyptian terrorist and 9/11 hijacker (1968–2001)
One of the smallest self-replicating organisms known, this cell-wall-lacking bacterium was originally called the 'Eaton agent' after being cultivated in chicken eggs in 1944 — what organism is it?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
This British-American historian, a senior fellow at Stanford's Hoover Institution, writes on financial history and holds notably favorable views of the British Empire — who is he?
Known as holy basil and sacred within the Vaishnava tradition of Hinduism, which aromatic herb is widely used in Ayurvedic tea?
Ocimum tenuiflorum: Species of flowering plant.
Also called a steer or bullock, and usually yoked in pairs, which castrated male bovine has long served as a draft animal for ploughing and hauling?
Ox: Common bovine draft and riding animal.
Named Pisum sativum by Carl Linnaeus in 1753, this pulse crop's pods are botanically a fruit containing seeds with green or yellow cotyledons — what vegetable is it?
Pea: Species of plant with edible seeds.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Downgraded from planet to dwarf in 2006 when astronomers adopted a new definition, this Kuiper belt object orbits beyond Neptune—what celestial body is it?
Pluto: Largest dwarf planet. Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
Though often mistaken for a true antelope, this hoofed North American mammal is actually the last living member of its own family, and its closest relatives are the giraffe and okapi — which animal?

Pronghorn: Species of North American hoofed mammal. The pronghorn (UK:, US:) (Antilocapra americana) is a species of artiodactyl (even-toed, hoofed) mammal indigenous to interior western and central North America.
Named for its four heads, this large muscle group covers the front of the thigh and is the sole muscle that extends the knee — what is it?
Quadriceps: Group of human leg muscle.

Also known as Willis–Ekbom disease, this neurological disorder creates an overwhelming urge to move one's limbs, especially when at rest, often described as a crawling or tingling sensation — what's the condition called?
Restless legs syndrome: Medical condition. There is often an unpleasant feeling in the legs that improves temporarily by moving them.
Operating under the alias 'Dread Pirate Roberts,' this American created and ran the dark-web marketplace Silk Road until his 2013 FBI arrest — who is he?
Ross Ulbricht: American cybercriminal founder of Silk Road (born 1984)
Also called a green onion, this mild Allium vegetable has a slender green stem but never develops a bulb like its garlic and leek relatives — what is it?
Scallion: Edible vegetable of various species in the genus Allium.
This body of religious law, drawn from the Qur'an and hadith, refers to immutable divine law — distinct from fiqh, its human interpretation by scholars. What is it?
Sharia: Islamic law. Approaches to Sharia in the 21st century vary widely, and the role and mutability of Sharia in a changing world has become an increasingly debated topic in Islam.
A hygroscopic crystalline powder (formula NaNO2) and the most industrially important salt of its kind, this compound is most familiar to us cured into processed meats. What is it?
Sodium nitrite: Chemical compound. It is a white to slightly yellowish crystalline powder that is very soluble in water and is hygroscopic.
This Polish-American DuPont chemist invented a super-strong polymer fiber and became the fourth woman ever inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame — who was she?
Stephanie Kwolek: American chemist who invented Kevlar (1923–2014)
Commonly known as fainting, this fast-onset, short-duration loss of consciousness and muscle strength is typically caused by a sudden drop in blood flow to the brain — what's the medical term?
Syncope (medicine): Transient loss of consciousness and postural tone.
Also called oxolane, this colorless, water-miscible cyclic ether is a versatile solvent and polymer precursor — and an isomer of butanone. Abbreviated with three letters, what is it?
Discovered in Cornwall in 1791 and named after the Titans of Greek myth, this corrosion-resistant transition metal shrugs off seawater, aqua regia, and chlorine alike — what is it?
Titanium: Chemical element with atomic number 22 (Ti)

These simple-looking marine invertebrates surprise biologists: their tadpole-like larvae sport a notochord and dorsal nerve cord, making them startlingly close kin to vertebrates. What are these chordates?
Tunicate: Marine animals, subphylum of chordates.
Described from Mongolian fossils in 1924 and smaller than relatives like Deinonychus, which feathered, sickle-clawed dinosaur genus roamed Late Cretaceous Asia?
Velociraptor: Genus of Late Cretaceous dinosaur. The type species is V. mongoliensis, named and described in 1924.
First cultivated in the Fertile Crescent around 9600 BC, this cereal grass is grown on more land worldwide than any other food crop — which grain?
Wheat: Genus of grass cultivated for grain. Wheat is a group of wild and domesticated grasses of the genus Triticum.
Nicknamed the 'Sleeping Dragon' during his years in seclusion, this strategist was sought out three times by Liu Bei and helped engineer victory at the Battle of Red Cliffs — who is he?
Zhuge Liang: Chinese statesman and strategist (181–234)
The symbol for vanadium is V. Vanadium is a chemical element; it has symbol V and atomic number 23.
What is the chemical symbol for gallium?
The symbol for gallium is Ga. Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

In what year did James Gandolfini die?
James Gandolfini: James John Gandolfini (Italian: [ɡandolˈfiːni]; September 18, 1961 – June 19, 2013) was an American actor.

Alien is a 1979 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Dan O'Bannon, based on a story by O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett.

Wonka is a 2023 musical fantasy film directed by Paul King, who co-wrote the screenplay with Simon Farnaby.
In what year was Madame Web first released?
Madame Web is a 2024 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics character.
In what year was Godzilla Minus One first released?
Godzilla Minus One: It is the 37th film in the Godzilla franchise, the 33rd film thereof produced by Toho, and the fifth installment in the Reiwa era.
In what year was Thor: The Dark World first released?
Thor: The Dark World: 2013. It is the sequel to Thor (2011) and the eighth film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).
